item.title: Iran may be working on biological weapons, Trump says
item.description: President Trump told Fox News there are indications Iran may be working on biological or chemical weapons as the war drags on toward its ninth month.

item.title: Photos, videos show devastating South Florida flooding
item.description: Significant flooding devastated some South Florida communities this week.

item.title: Beloved hippo Fiona dies days after swallowing hat
item.description: Fiona the hippo, who survived being born prematurely and rose to global fame, has died, the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden announced Thursday.

item.title: Senate passes bipartisan permitting bill designed to boost energy projects
item.description: The Senate approved a long-sought bipartisan permitting reform bill on Thursday, following a major breakthrough on legislation that aims to cut costs by ramping up the speed of infrastructure and energy projects.

item.title: Army delays detonation in Iowa that could send toxic dust into Illinois
item.description: The U.S. Army has delayed plans to detonate unstable explosives at a munition plant in Iowa, amid concerns about the risks of a plume of dust containing toxic lead particles that could spread across parts of Iowa and Illinois.

item.title: DOJ moves to dismiss lawsuit over Alaska Senate race
item.description: The Trump administration is moving to effectively drop its legal challenge to Democrat Mary Peltola's win in Alaska's Senate race.

item.title: Behind the scenes look of Huntington Beach's new e-bike safety program
item.description: Sgt. Brad Smith, of the Huntington Beach Police Department, said the main concern is safety. The e-bike program is meant to decrease injuries and deaths on the road.

item.title: White House national cyber director leaving his post
item.description: White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross will be leaving his position, a White House official told CBS News.

item.title: Marine Corps hero under federal investigation
item.description: Retired Sgt. Maj. Bradley Kasal, whose bloodied visage was depicted in an iconic Iraq War photo, is under investigation stemming from his tenure as a high school JROTC instructor.

item.title: Judge further delays Trump's plan for D.C. arch
item.description: A federal judge is putting President Trump's plans for a triumphal arch on hold for another two weeks. With a Democrat-led Congress coming into session in 2027, lawmakers could throw a wrench into Mr. Trump's plans for the arch and more. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: No major agreements from Trump summit with Putin, Xi
item.description: President Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin held a historic summit this week in China, but they didn't reach any major agreements. Zeke Miller, deputy Washington bureau chief at the Associated Press, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Anthropic's 7 co-founders now worth about $20 billion each after record IPO
item.description: Anthropic on Thursday posted the largest IPO on record and ended the day with shares up 17%, putting its valuation at $1.7 trillion. Miles Kruppa, technology correspondent for the Economist, joins CBS News with more.

item.title: What to know after hackers target Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase
item.description: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard announced Thursday that a ransomware group hacked into third-party systems used by the firms and accessed data from potentially thousands of customers. CBS News' Ann Berry has more.

item.title: Susan Smith denied parole again, 32 years after drowning sons
item.description: More than 30 years after killing her two young sons, Susan Smith was denied parole for a second time on Thursday. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul has more.

item.title: Trump to speak Friday about summit with Xi and Putin; Zelenskyy meets with U.S. envoys
item.description: President Trump will speak Friday about the meeting he had this week with Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping. CBS News' Aidan Stretch has more on that and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's meeting with U.S. envoys and European leaders.

item.title: Husband of American detained in Russia says case was not mentioned during Trump meeting with Putin
item.description: Harold Jezler is the husband of Olga Jezler, an American who has been detained in Russia for over four years. He joins "The Takeout" to share details on his wife's condition and call for her safe return.

item.title: Trump calls Putin his friend at summit, prompting backlash from some world leaders
item.description: President Trump insisted that Russian President Vladimir Putin wants to end his war with Ukraine as the two leaders met with Chinese President Xi Jinping. But Putin later told reporters he plans to halt negotiations with the country he invaded in 2022. Mr. Trump also called Putin his friend, sparking a rebuke from the prime minister of Poland. Nancy Cordes and Anna Coren report.

item.title: Extended interview: Rahm Emanuel on his presidential aspirations, Trump's trilateral summit, more
item.description: Former White House chief of staff and Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel speaks with Major Garrett about President Trump's summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, artificial intelligence and whether he might run for president.

item.title: 2-year-old who went missing in desert found by volunteer
item.description: Jay Stewart was overcome with emotion during a news conference as he recalled the moment he found a missing 2-year-old curled up under a bush just after midnight on Wednesday.

item.title: Inside Shenzhen, the Chinese city that grew to twice the size of NYC in less than a generation
item.description: Tony Dokoupil takes a walk around Shenzhen, the bustling Chinese city that just hosted President Trump, and learns about its people and culture.

item.title: Video shows moments after missing 2-year-old girl found in remote Arizona desert
item.description: A 2-year-old girl was rescued after spending seven hours alone in the Arizona desert. Carter Evans reports.

item.title: Here are the GTA 6 songs you'll hear cruising around Vice City
item.description: Grand Theft Auto 6 players carry out missions to songs by artists such as Cardi B, Lana Del Rey and Travis Scott.

item.title: Musk says he's "not MAGA," feels "foolish" about midterm spending
item.description: After opening his wallet to assist GOP candidates in the 2026 midterms, billionaire Elon Musk said Wednesday he feels "pretty foolish" about spending hundreds of millions of dollars in the race.

item.title: Rahm Emanuel on possibly running for president in 2028
item.description: Rahm Emanuel, who was President Obama's former chief of staff and two-term mayor of Chicago, talks with Major Garrett about a potential 2028 presidential run.

item.title: 11/19: CBS Evening News
item.description: Dangerous flooding batters Florida; Market down as Anthropic goes public.

item.title: Consumers stock doomsday pantries as tech outages cause jitters
item.description: Companies such as Costco and Walmart are seeing a surge in sales for generators, canned goods and other disaster-preparedness staples.

item.title: Trump pardons deceased MLB slugger Pete Rose
item.description: President Trump said Thursday he has granted a "Complete and Total Pardon" to Pete Rose, MLB's late all-time hits leader who was banned from the league for gambling.

item.title: 11/19: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Trump meets with Putin and Xi in historic summit; Anthropic goes public with record IPO.

item.title: Woman runs 7 marathons while pregnant this year: "I am very stubborn"
item.description: Deirdre Keane, a 38-year-old nurse and management consultant, achieved her goal of completing all seven World Marathon Majors while pregnant with her first child.

item.title: Meet the 19 new senators set to be sworn in to Congress
item.description: From a former wheelchair basketball Paralympian to a Methodist pastor and one senator returning after defeat, the new class hails from different backgrounds and parts of the country.
